_comment: The NULL CLASS for the hvi-icd-concepts index. Every phrase here is ordinary call conversation that is NOT a medical disclosure. They are embedded and indexed alongside the condition surface forms; when a caller's utterance retrieves one of these as its nearest neighbour, the classifier's answer is 'this is not a condition' - which a pure condition index could never say. Grown from REAL failures: each section lists garbage that a live call turned into a confident diagnosis (Epilepsy from 'Here they are.', Parkinson's from 'नहीं', Osteoarthritis from 'Jardiance.'). Add to this file whenever a conversational phrase classifies as a disease; never remove entries without checking the git log for which call added them.

phrases: which disease are you talking about?
kis bimari ki baat kar rahe ho?
किस बीमारी के बारे में बात कर रही हैं आप?
आप कहना क्या चाह रहे हैं?
यह कॉल रिकॉर्ड की जा रही है
this call is not being recorded

distractors._comment: Bare measurements and dates only. Time-AGO phrases (paanch saal pehle) were here and swallowed a real disclosure - 'कैंसर था पाँच साल पहले' retrieved the distractor 'पाँच साल पहले' as its nearest neighbour and the cancer was nulled. Durations live inside genuine disclosures too often to be distractors.

A bare drug name is not a condition disclosure: 'Jardiance.' (a garbled height answer) classified confidently to a disease because drug names embed near their indication. Medications are handled by the treatment follow-ups and the med-consistency check, where they carry real signal; here they must not mint a diagnosis on their own.

A HABIT IS NOT A DIAGNOSIS. The form asks about tobacco and alcohol on their own items (A400-A430) because a habit is priced as a risk factor, not recorded as a disease - but 'smoke' retrieved COPD's colloquial synonym "smoker's lung" at 0.8141, came back CORROBORATED by the graph, and therefore took the no-read-back path: answering yes to 'do you use tobacco?' silently wrote Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease onto an underwriting record, with nobody ever asked. Found by tests/test_positive_disclosures.py. Only bare habit words belong here; 'smoker's lung' itself is a real disclosure and stays an exact J44 synonym, which the neptune_exact_synonym path resolves at 1.0 ahead of any of this.

A TEST IS NOT A DIAGNOSIS. A600/A610 exist to capture an abnormal investigation in the caller's own words, and that free text is what the underwriter reads - but the name of the test embeds next to the disease it investigates, so 'liver function test' retrieved Cirrhosis of Liver at 0.7948 (matchedVia the literal label) and asked a layperson 'is that Cirrhosis of Liver?'. The read-back does stop these reaching the record, but only if the caller knows enough to say no, and a leading clinical question is not one to put to someone who just told you their enzymes were high. Nulling them costs nothing: the verbatim answer is still recorded on the item. An OPERATION is different and belongs here only while the graph has no code for what was operated on: 'gallstone surgery' was nulled here until K80 Gallstones was added, and is now a real disclosure that resolves properly - the same will be true of appendix and cataract surgery if those conditions are ever added.
